directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, since this Bolivian-Peruvian baccatum type needs a long warm season to fully ripen its pendant, 3-5 inch pods. Fruit matures from green through orange to a deep brick-red, carrying a fast-hitting heat (roughly 20,000-30,000 Scoville units) that fades quickly and leaves a sweet, fruity aftertaste. Thin walls make it well suited to drying or blending into fresh aji sauces once red-ripe; harvest continuously to extend production into fall.

common_name: Aji Fantasy Pepper (Finnish-Bred Translucent Yellow Baccatum)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks ahead of the last frost; this compact, high-yielding baccatum variety matures faster than most aji types.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks ahead of the last frost; this compact, high-yielding baccatum variety was developed in Finland and matures faster than most aji types, making it a good option for shorter growing seasons. The roughly 2 inch, bonnet-shaped pods ripen to a translucent yellow and deliver a mild-to-medium heat (about 5,000-10,000 Scoville units) with pronounced tropical sweetness. Stake plants as they load up with fruit, and pick continuously to keep the heavily branching bushes producing.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; stake or cage the tall, rangy plants and provide consistent moisture through fruit set.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; this modern baccatum selection, first found as a natural mutation of a South American aji type, needs the long, warm season typical of the species to size up. The glossy, peach-colored pods bring a habanero-adjacent heat wrapped in intense sweetness, with tropical and citrus notes that make them popular fresh in salads and ceviche or fermented into hot sauce. Plants grow tall and rangy, so stake or cage them and provide consistent moisture through fruit set.

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, and give this vigorous baccatum plenty of vertical support since it can top 5 feet in a single season.

directions: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, and give this vigorous baccatum plenty of vertical support — it can top 5 feet in a single season. Fruits begin lime green and ripen through a striking peach-and-red striped pattern that stays fairly stable from seed, with a Scoville range of roughly 25,000-100,000 that leans hotter than most other aji types. The flavor combines sweet, fruity, citrus, and stone-fruit notes, making it a favorite for colorful hot sauces and fresh garnishes.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; provide staking for the tall, productive plants and harvest regularly to prolong the season.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost. This variety arose as an off-type selection within Sugar Rush Stripey plantings and ripens to a solid, glossy red rather than the parent's stripe pattern, with a milder heat range of about 5,000-45,000 Scoville units. It shares the same sweet, tropical-fruit flavor profile as its siblings and works well fresh, fermented, or dried. Provide staking for the tall, productive plants and harvest regularly to prolong the season.
